data.narrative:
Osaro is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $86.8M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of three same-stage, same-sector private companies (Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity) alongside one public comparable, reflecting the nascent but active market for frontier robotics technology.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $87M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $165M. Peer-median analysis across the three private comparables—valued between $1.6B and $2.0B—produces a $1.8B implied valuation. The disparity reflects stage-to-stage advancement: peer companies have progressed further or secured capital at higher multiples.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $140M to $2.0B, with a median of $957M. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty around whether Osaro more closely mirrors the $87M base raised (suggesting earlier traction assessment) or the $1.6B–$2.0B peer band (assuming comparable progress and market positioning). Key uncertainties include revenue traction relative to peers, capital efficiency post-Series A, and whether the peer set adequately reflects Osaro's technological differentiation and addressable market capture. A narrowed range would require additional transparency on unit economics and pipeline maturity.
